correction_controls: Shared nested tuple key at successive depths below declared depth/key_items bounds.
Native-equal bool/int/finite-float keys and nested tuple variants, preserving collisions/refusals.
Rejected key preflight retains exact raw Document/work/wire/first fault and full available prefix without repair or retry.

finding.argument: The parser caches one native tuple per unique key node, then passes that tuple to ordinary dictionary membership/insertion. Those operations invoke native tuple hashing. Unique-node key_items and interval-128 Work steps do not count the recursively repeated child hash occurrences. Thus the proposed generic bounded-work argument lacks a bound or checkpoints for this native operation.
finding.location: Document._key and Document._parse native dictionary collision validation
finding.scope: This is a generic accepted-wire/input resource obligation. It does not prove that the fixed original cohort contains such keys or that every shared-owner design fails.

primary_source.read_method: Read-only official upstream Source via web open; no code executed.

primary_source.runtime_scope: This is upstream CPython3.12.14 Source evidence. It does not independently prove that the pinned custom runtime binary contains an unmodified tuplehash; no binary or runtime probe was made. The implementation must discharge its actual runtime resource obligation.

prospective_unrun_recipe.expected_successor: Either preflight and charge a conservative expanded-key occurrence bound before any native tuple hash/equality, or implement complete charged canonical key equality without recursive native tuple hashing. Preserve exact bool/int/float/tuple collision semantics.
prospective_unrun_recipe.hash_argument: Upstream CPython tuplehash recursively invokes PyObject_Hash for every child and does not cache a tuple hash. For this shared family the recursive hash work obeys \(H(k+1)\geq 2H(k)\), despite linear DAG size. No Work.step is called by that builtin recursion.
prospective_unrun_recipe.mathematical_definition: \(t_0=(),\quad t_{i+1}=(t_i,t_i).\) Use the full hashable tuple \(t_k\) as one dictionary key in a complete strict canonical DAG.
prospective_unrun_recipe.quota_requirement: Use a declared depth/key_items/node limit permitting the selected finite depth; the wire and all ordinary grammar remain complete. No fixture, wire generation, hashing, timing or simulator was performed here.
prospective_unrun_recipe.structural_size: The DAG has linearly many unique tuple nodes and two child references per positive level. Document._key preserves sharing and counts only those unique keys, so materializing the tuple graph is linear in the depth.
